title: Hummus
subtitle: Classic chickpea and tahini dip
excerpt: Smooth, creamy hummus made from chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon juice, and garlic. Finished with a drizzle of olive oil and smoked paprika. Far better than the shop-bought version.

recipe.sourceNotes: Hummus bi tahini (chickpeas with sesame paste) is one of the oldest and most widely eaten dishes in the Middle East, with roots extending back to at least the thirteenth century in Egypt and the Levant. Today the dish is claimed by many countries including Lebanon, Israel, Palestine, and Egypt, and the question of origin is politically charged. The dish spread globally from the 1960s onwards. The key to smooth, creamy hummus is the ratio of tahini to chickpeas and, less intuitively, the peeling of the chickpeas. Removing the skins from each chickpea before blending produces a noticeably smoother result; it is tedious but worthwhile for a special occasion. The other technique is to blend the tahini and lemon juice together first, creating a thick, creamy tahini paste, before adding the chickpeas: this produces a lighter, creamier texture than blending everything at once. Tinned chickpeas work well; dried chickpeas cooked from scratch produce a slightly better flavour and texture.

content.text: Blend the tahini and lemon juice together first until thick and creamy before adding the chickpeas. This emulsification step creates a lighter, airier hummus than blending everything together. For a very smooth result, run the blender for at least 3 minutes after adding the chickpeas, scraping down the sides regularly. Adjust the consistency with ice-cold water: a few tablespoons of cold water added while the blender is running produces a lighter, fluffier texture.

items.preparation: 400 g tins, drained; reserve the liquid

content.text: Put the tahini and lemon juice in a food processor or blender. Process for 1 minute until thick and creamy. Add the garlic, salt, and cumin. Process for 30 seconds.

Add the drained chickpeas and olive oil. Process for 2 to 3 minutes until very smooth, stopping to scrape down the sides. Add 3 to 4 tablespoons of cold water while blending until the hummus is creamy and just dropping from a spoon. Taste and adjust the lemon and salt.
Spread onto a plate or into a bowl. Make a well in the centre with the back of a spoon and pour in a generous drizzle of olive oil. Dust with smoked paprika. Serve with flatbread or warm pitta.
